sentences.text: Alistipes onderdonkii was proposed as a species of Gram-negative, strictly anaerobic, pigment-producing rods related to Alistipes finegoldii, from bacteria of human origin.
Its separation from A. finegoldii rested on about 3% divergence in the 16S ribosomal RNA gene together with distinguishable biochemical characteristics.

A case report describes it as a rare anaerobic Gram-negative bacillus that forms part of the normal gastrointestinal microbiota but has emerged as an opportunistic pathogen in immunocompromised individuals.
In faecal metagenomes from 96 Mongolian participants, Alistipes onderdonkii was reported to be significantly reduced in overweight individuals.
